body:
## Problem

link-cli has three implementations (C# in `csharp/`, Rust in `rust/`, and a JavaScript/WASM web workbench in `js/`) and one workflow per stack. The workflows do not wait for each other, nothing in CI checks that the C# and Rust implementations stay at parity, `main` has no protection, and the open pull requests are stale or red. This is the audit of link-cli against the standard in link-assistant/router#759 (requirements 3, 4, 6 and 8), the shared pipeline templates and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Only missing or broken practices are listed.

## Findings

1. **Rust and C# CI/CD are not gated on JavaScript.** `.github/workflows/rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and `wasm.yml` each trigger on their own `push`/`pull_request` and none has `workflow_run` or a cross-workflow `needs:`. The JavaScript unit tests (`npm run test:js`) run only in `wasm.yml` (line 81), which itself builds the Rust WASM crate. A Rust or C# change starts the full Rust matrix and the C# matrix in parallel with the JavaScript checks. Evidence from the run list: for the Dependabot branch `dependabot/nuget/...` on 2026-10-09 `C# CI/CD Pipeline`, `Dependencies`, `Docs` and `Security` all started at the same second (03:49:35Z).
2. **No parity gate between the implementations.** There is no parity manifest and no checker. The only parity artefacts are one Rust test file (`rust/tests/query_processor_csharp_parity_tests.rs`) and prose in `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`. Nothing fails CI when a feature changes in C# but not in Rust (or the reverse). The `js/` package is a React/WASM workbench over the Rust crate, and no document states which features it covers. Path filters make this worse: `rust.yml` runs only for `rust/**` and `csharp.yml` only for C# paths, so a one-sided change never triggers the other stack's checks.
3. **`main` is not protected.** `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection` returns 404 "Branch not protected", and `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/rulesets` returns an empty list. No required checks, so a red PR can be merged and the three stages are not enforced.
4. **Eight stale pull requests from 2025 are still open.** #36, #37, #38, #39, #40, #41 (all 2025-09-10), #49 (2025-09-10) and #57 (2025-09-15). They are about 13 months old, none has a CI check result, and each duplicates an open issue (#30-#35, #18, #56, #59, #60). There is no stale policy or workflow that closes or flags them.
5. **The only active PR and the default branch are red.** PR #109 (Dependabot, NuGet group, opened 2026-10-09) fails `C# CI/CD Pipeline`: `LinoProtocolCodecTests.ReferencesAreQuotedOnlyWhenNeeded` and `TextMessagesAreDotStuffed` fail on Windows and in "Simulate Fresh Merge", which reports a semantic merge conflict. The `Dependencies` workflow also failed on `main` on 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09 (daily scheduled runs) and nobody has acted on it.
6. **Files and workflows from the shared templates are missing.** Compared with `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` and `js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`, link-cli has none of: `.github/workflows/workflows.yml` (actionlint with shellcheck), `.github/zizmor.yml` (workflow security lint), `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md`. A grep for `actionlint` and `zizmor` in `.github` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` finds nothing. `js/` has no ESLint or Prettier configuration and no lint script.
7. **No agent rules or push gate.** There is no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `.github/CODEOWNERS`, so the single-pusher rule for CI/CD fixes from router#759 requirement 4 is not documented here, and nobody is auto-requested to review.

## Requirements

1. Add a stage gate: the Rust and C# jobs run only after the JavaScript stage (lint, tests, parity check) has succeeded for the same commit, using one entry workflow with `needs:` or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha`. A cancelled or skipped JavaScript run must not start Rust or C#. Testable: a PR with a failing `npm run test:js` shows no Rust or C# job started.
2. Move `npm run test:js` out of the Rust-dependent `wasm.yml` into a JavaScript stage that does not need `wasm-pack` or Rust, and keep the WASM build in the gated stage.
3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`) listing each CLI/library feature with its C#, Rust and JavaScript implementation status and test evidence, plus a checker script that fails when an implementation changes a feature entry without the others. Run it in every stack's workflow with no path filter that can skip it.
4. Add shared golden fixtures that both the C# and the Rust test suites must pass, and a CI job that fails if either suite does not load them.
5. Document in `docs/` which features the `js/` workbench implements and which it delegates to the Rust WASM crate.
6. Enable branch protection or a ruleset on `main` that requires the JavaScript, Rust and C# stage checks and blocks merging when any is red. Testable: `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection` returns 200.
7. Triage PRs #36-#41, #49 and #57: close them, or rebase and run CI. Add a stale workflow (or equivalent) so PRs idle for more than 60 days are flagged and then closed.
8. Fix or close PR #109 so the NuGet group updates are merged green (or held with a linked issue per the `Dependencies` workflow rules), and make the scheduled `Dependencies` failure on `main` open or update a tracking issue instead of staying silently red.
9. Add `workflows.yml` (actionlint with shellcheck), `.github/zizmor.yml` and the CodeQL config from the templates, and fix any findings they report. Add ESLint and Prettier (or document why not) for `js/`.
10. Add `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) and `.github/CODEOWNERS`, including the single-pusher rule: one sub-agent pushes only after all failures of the last run are fixed, and no push happens while a run is in progress on the same branch.
11. Add a CI check (extend `.github/scripts/workflow-policy.test.mjs`) that fails if any workflow can start Rust or C# jobs without the JavaScript gate.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (standard this audit applies)
- Existing link-cli issues: none cover CI/CD, gating or parity. #91 (rename), #108 (JS/TS adapter) and #110 (Rust import scaling) are unrelated; #18, #30-#35, #56, #59, #60 are the issues duplicated by the stale PRs in finding 4.
- Partly in place already: `.github/scripts/workflow-policy.test.mjs` (timeouts, permissions, concurrency) and the `fresh-merge` jobs.

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: Adopt the JavaScript-first CI gate, cross-language parity gate and missing repository hygiene in link-cli
